business_model.claim: MFA's structure and capital retention are governed by REIT tax rules requiring distribution of at least 90% of annual REIT taxable income and by the Investment Company Act 40% Test limiting investment securities to less than 40% of adjusted total assets.
quotes: In order to maintain our qualification as a REIT, we must comply with a number of requirements under federal tax law, including that we must distribute at least 90% of our annual REIT taxable income to our stockholders.

We are a holding company and conduct our real estate finance businesses primarily through wholly-owned subsidiaries, so as to maintain an exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (or the Investment Company Act) by ensuring that less than 40% of the value of our total assets, exclusive of U.S. Government securities and cash items (which we refer to as our adjusted total assets for Investment Company Act purposes), on an unconsolidated basis, consist of “investment securities” as defined by the Investment Company Act.

competitive_position.claim: MFA Financial is an internally-managed residential mortgage REIT that has distributed over $5 billion in dividends since its 1998 IPO.
quotes: We are an internally-managed real estate investment trust (or REIT).
MFA Financial, Inc. (NYSE: MFA) is a leading specialty finance company that invests in residential mortgage loans, residential mortgage-backed securities and other real estate assets.
MFA has distributed over $5 billion in dividends to stockholders since its initial public offering in 1998.

competitive_position.claim: MFA held $13.5 billion in total assets at September 30, 2026, anchored by 64% in residential whole loans and 29% in Agency MBS.
quotes: At September 30, 2026, we had total assets of approximately $13.5 billion, of which $8.7 billion, or 64%, represented residential whole loans.
In addition, at September 30, 2026, we had approximately $3.9 billion, or 29%, of total assets invested in investments in Agency MBS.

competitive_position.claim: MFA owns Lima One, a nationwide business purpose loan originator and servicer that has funded over $7.3 billion of loans since its July 2021 acquisition.
quotes: Through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Lima One Capital, LLC (together with its parent company, Lima One Holdings, LLC, “Lima One”), a leading nationwide originator and servicer of Business purpose loans (or BPLs), which we acquired on July 1, 2021, we originate and service BPLs for real estate investors.
This includes $0.9 billion of loans originated by our wholly-owned subsidiary, Lima One, which has funded more than $7.3 billion of loans since July 2021, when we fully acquired Lima One.
At December 31, 2025, we had 307 employees, including 250 employees working in our Lima One subsidiary.

competitive_position.claim: Lima One expanded distribution by selling $212.9 million of single-family rental loans in 2025 and $94.8 million in the third quarter of 2026, while launching a wholesale channel and relaunching multifamily lending in 2026.
quotes: During 2025, Lima One sold $212.9 million of recently originated single-family rental loans to third parties and realized gains of $6.1 million.
We believe that these sales to third parties help to strengthen Lima One’s franchise value, create additional distribution channels to accommodate future growth, and enhance returns.
In early 2026, we relaunched multifamily lending and began funding loans through our newly established wholesale channel, which represent two key areas of growth for Lima One.
Asset dispositions included $94.8 million of proceeds from recently-originated single-family rental (SFR) loans, generating a $2.4 million gain on sale.

competitive_position.claim: MFA uses loan securitizations to lock in non-recourse, fixed-rate funding and reduce margin risk, reaching approximately $5.9 billion of securitized debt at September 30, 2026.
quotes: While market conditions have improved and recession risks have moderated, we have maintained our emphasis on preserving sufficient liquidity, prudently managing our interest rate exposure, and using loan securitizations to minimize our exposure to margin risk.
During 2025, we completed five Non-QM loan securitizations with unpaid principal balance (or UPB) of loans sold of $1.8 billion.
These securitizations provide longer term, non-recourse, fixed rate financing.
MFA completed one securitization during the quarter collateralized by $446.5 million UPB of loans, bringing its total securitized debt to approximately $5.9 billion.

competitive_position.claim: Management positions underwriting around low origination LTVs and discounted purchases of seasoned RPL/NPL loans, achieving a 64% weighted average LTV across residential whole loans at September 30, 2026.
quotes: With respect to investments in Business purpose and Non-QM loans, we believe that sound underwriting standards, including low LTVs at origination, significantly mitigate our risk of loss.

Further, we believe the discounted purchase prices paid on Seasoned RPL/NPL loans mitigate our risk of loss in the event that we receive less than 100% of the unpaid principal balance of these investments.
60+ day delinquencies (measured as a percentage of UPB) for MFA’s residential loan portfolio decreased to 6.7% at September 30, 2026 from 7.0% at June 30, 2026.

competitive_position.claim: MFA faces intense competition from larger, less-regulated institutions that can bid up residential mortgage asset prices and compress investment yields.
quotes: We believe that our principal competitors in the business of acquiring and holding residential mortgage assets of the types in which we invest are financial institutions, such as banks, specialty finance companies, insurance companies, institutional investors, including mutual funds and pension funds, hedge funds and other mortgage REITs.
Some of these entities may not be subject to the same regulatory constraints (i.e., REIT compliance or maintaining an exemption under the Investment Company Act) as we are.
In addition, many of these entities have greater financial resources and access to capital than we have.

The existence of these entities, as well as the possibility of additional entities forming in the future, may increase the competition for the acquisition of residential mortgage assets, resulting in higher prices and lower yields on such assets.

competitive_position.claim: Maintaining REIT tax qualification and the Investment Company Act 40% Test restricts MFA's asset mix, hedging flexibility, and capital retention compared with non-REIT competitors.
quotes: In order to maintain our qualification as a REIT, we must comply with a number of requirements under federal tax law, including that we must distribute at least 90% of our annual REIT taxable income to our stockholders.

We are a holding company and conduct our real estate finance businesses primarily through wholly-owned subsidiaries, so as to maintain an exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (or the Investment Company Act) by ensuring that less than 40% of the value of our total assets, exclusive of U.S. Government securities and cash items (which we refer to as our adjusted total assets for Investment Company Act purposes), on an unconsolidated basis, consist of “investment securities” as defined by the Investment Company Act.
Maintaining our exemption from registration under the Investment Company Act significantly limits our operations.
Complying with REIT requirements may limit our ability to hedge effectively and may cause us to incur tax liabilities.

competitive_position.claim: Interest rate spikes, spread widening, and leveraged mark-to-market exposure threaten MFA's net interest spread and book value, driving a (10.6)% total economic return in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: Therefore, a period of high interest rates and flattening or inverted yield curves, such as the conditions experienced during the past few years, which may continue in 2026, presents challenges on our ability to effectively manage the risks associated with our business operations, including interest rate, prepayment, financing, liquidity and credit risks, while maintaining our qualification as a REIT.

“The third quarter was challenging for mortgage investors with Treasury yields spiking across the curve and heightened volatility sending spreads wider,” said Craig Knutson, MFA’s Chief Executive Officer.
Total economic return was (10.6)% for the third quarter.
MFA incurred a GAAP net loss to common stockholders and participating securities for the third quarter of $(122.4) million, or $(1.19) per basic and diluted common share.

competitive_position.claim: Geographic concentration in key states, borrower refinancing dependency, and third-party counterparty and valuation-model limitations threaten loan credit performance and asset recoveries.
quotes: For example, we have significant exposure in California, Florida, Texas, Georgia and New York.
Our investments in residential whole loans are difficult to value and are dependent upon the borrower’s ability to service or refinance their debt.

We are subject to counterparty risk and may be unable to seek indemnity or require counterparties to repurchase residential whole loans if they breach representations and warranties, which could cause us to suffer losses.

The use of models in connection with the valuation and credit losses of our assets subjects us to potential risks in the event that such models are incorrect, misleading or based on incomplete information.

competitive_position.claim: Potential U.S. mortgage finance reform affecting Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac and evolving CFPB rules threaten MFA's Agency MBS valuations, borrower refinancing, and compliance costs.
quotes: While the likelihood of enactment of major mortgage finance system reform in the short term remains uncertain, it is possible that the adoption of any such reforms could adversely affect the types of assets we can buy, the costs of these assets and our business operations.
In addition, any decline in the value of securities issued by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac may affect the value of our Agency MBS and Residential whole loans in general.

We believe that the Dodd-Frank Act and the regulations promulgated thereunder are likely to continue to increase the economic and compliance costs for participants in the mortgage and securitization industries, including us.

competitive_position.claim: MFA faces an upcoming executive leadership transition as CEO Craig Knutson retires effective June 30, 2027, creating execution risk given its dependence on key personnel.
quotes: We are dependent on our executive officers and other key personnel for our success.
As previously announced, Craig Knutson will retire as Chief Executive Officer, effective June 30, 2027.
Bryan Wulfsohn will join the Board on January 1, 2027 and become Chief Executive Officer on July 1, 2027.
In addition, Andrew Kail will join MFA as Senior Vice President and Chief Investment Officer, effective January 1, 2027.
